CLAIM: the 18 knobs (perf_metrics.flaky_*, slo.*, store.stale_index_days, upstream_gh.error_max, worktree.stash_*) are defined in the code's config defaults but absent from the upgrade manifest replay, so test_the_current_code_has_exactly_the_knobs_and_event_kinds_the_manifest_gives_it fails. FALSIFIER: one of the 18 keys already announced in the manifest/fragments, or lint() reporting a non-knob_added change. PROBE: ddflow version lint -> reported exactly 18 knob_added:*, 0 non-knob; after writing the 18 fragments it reports '0 unmanifested, 0 waived'. VERDICT CONFIRMED.

Applied rules governing these files: r-derive-dont-store (fragments derive from lint diff, never hand-edited), B-upgrade.2-changes.2-lint (one <kind>.<key>.toml per change under unreleased/), D-upgrade-manifest-lint (lint() replay must equal the code). Fragments written via UM.Unmanifested.fragment() pre-fill; operator refine of why/effect remains their own.

chunk_findings.detail: The `why` values are stored truncated mid-token with a literal ellipsis, so an upgrade consumer printing these notes (or a snapshot that asserts the knob help text) gets incomplete reasons. `store.stale_index_days` ends at `garbage-coll...`, `upstream_gh.error_max` at `bef...`, `worktree.stash_retries` at `` `fatal:... ``, and `worktree.stash_retry_pause_s` at `the nth retr...`. Given those files as the unreleased upgrade record, the user-visible reason is not the full knob description the surface/explain tests require.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.store.stale_index_days.toml:5

data.probe: why is the fragment's ONE-LINE note by contract (Change.why: 'why is one line'; _WHY_CHARS=160) and its pre-fill is _first_sentence() truncated to that budget mid-word; the pre-fill text is the operator-mandated 'kind/key/new from the diff, why/effect the author refines'. The finding's mechanism claim is that a surface/explain snapshot asserts the FULL knob doc from why and would print the truncated note: refuted by 'uv run pytest tests/compat/test_surface.py::test_the_current_code_has_exactly_the_knobs_and_event_kinds_the_manifest_gives_it tests/test_upgrade_manifest_lint.py::test_this_tree_is_clean' -> 2 passed (3.11s), so no such snapshot asserts the full description. The mid-word cut is a _first_sentence budget artifact of the pre-existing pre-fill, not a defect in declaring the 18 knobs (all 18 keys and new defaults are correct).
